Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1224 PM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026

Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS EASTERN 
NORTH DAKOTA...NORTHWEST MINNESOTA...AND A SMALL PART OF NORTHEAST
SOUTH DAKOTA......

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered to scattered severe storms are expected across
eastern North Dakota, northwest Minnesota, and a small part of
northeast South Dakota Monday afternoon into evening. Severe wind
gusts and large hail will be the primary hazards. Isolated damaging
winds are possible from central and eastern South Dakota into
western Nebraska, in portions of the Mid-Atlantic into New England,
and southeast Arizona.

...Synopsis...
A progressive mid-level trough will move across the Northern Rockies
into the Northern Plains and upper Midwest Monday, with a belt of
unseasonably strong west to southwesterly flow overspreading
portions of the Dakotas into northern/central Minnesota. At the
surface, a cold front will shift eastward from the northern to the
central Plains, with a surface low moving across the Dakotas and a
secondary low across eastern Colorado.

Across the Northeast, a second mid-level trough will bring enhanced
southwesterly mid-level flow across the region. At the surface, a
warm front will lift northward across portions of New England with a
cold front advancing south and eastward as a surface low tracks into
Quebec.

...Northern and central Plains into the upper Mississippi Valley...
Elevated convection is likely to be ongoing at the start of the
period Monday morning across North Dakota into northern Minnesota.
These will pose some potential for large hail. Preceding morning
convection, steepening low to mid-level lapse rates along with
moistening with the strong southerly low-level jet should allow for
moderate to strong instability to redevelop by the afternoon.
Renewed thunderstorm development is expected along and ahead of the
cold front. Supercell wind profiles will be in place. Initially,
forecast soundings indicate lingering capping at the base of the
EML. This may erode through time but relatively warm  750-800 mb
levels may lead to fairly high LCLs, which may inhibit tornado
potential though large clockwise curved hodographs will be common.
The primary threats are expected to be large hail and damaging wind.

Capping at the base of an EML may remain further south, limiting
convection with southern extent into South Dakota and Nebraska.
Nonetheless, CAM guidance suggests signal for a few isolated
supercells to develop further south with potential for large hail
and damaging wind.

...New England into the Mid-Atlantic...
Widely scattered thunderstorm activity is expected to be ongoing
across the Mid-Atlantic and New England through much of the period.
Pockets of more focused daytime heating may result in moderate
instability by the afternoon. Aided by forcing for ascent attendant
to the short-wave trough, thunderstorms are expected to increase in
coverage and intensity through the afternoon along and ahead of the
front, namely in areas that experience greater air mass
destabilization. Steepening low-level lapse rates and the presence
of 35-45 kt of deep-layer shear may support embedded bowing segments
capable of damaging wind gusts.

...Southeast Arizona...
Easterly flow will favor thunderstorm development across the high
terrain in Southeast Arizona Monday. Widely scattered activity will
build across the high terrain and move into the lower valleys
through the afternoon and evening. A well mixed boundary layer,
moderate instability, and modest shear around 20-25 kts will support
potential for an organized cluster or two with potential to produce
damaging winds.

..Thornton.. 08/02/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0224 PM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026

Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
OF SOUTHEASTERN ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered severe storms capable of severe wind gusts appear
possible in southeast Arizona Tuesday afternoon and evening.

...Synopsis...
Broad troughing will continue across southern Canada into the
central US D3/Tuesday, with enhanced mid-level flow moving across
the Northern Rockies and Upper Great Lakes regions. A shortwave
trough will traverse the Mid-Missouri Valley late in the period as a
cold front shifts south and east from the Great Lakes/Midwest and
across the Central/Southern Plains.

...Southeast Arizona...
Strengthening easterly mid-level flow and lowering heights will aid
in thunderstorm development across the high terrain in southeastern
Arizona. Strengthening flow aloft will provide increased deep layer
shear for organization across the region. A deeply mixed and
moderately unstable air mass across the lower desert will support
potential for one or more clusters moving off the high terrain which
will be capable of damaging wind through the afternoon.

...Mid-Missouri Valley...
Several rounds of widely scattered thunderstorm activity is expected
across the Mid-Missouri Valley Tuesday. Elevated thunderstorm
activity will likely be ongoing near the start of the period near
the surface front. A corridor of moderate instability may develop
south of the front by afternoon from northeast KS into southern IA;
however, the absence of appreciable forcing mechanisms leads to
considerable uncertainty in whether any surface-based storms will
develop during the daylight hours. Better chances for development
will arrive with a shortwave trough passage late in the period. Poor
lapse rates and marginal instability leads to low confidence in
severe potential overnight, but a few stronger storms may produce
gusty winds and small hail given strong deep layer shear profiles.

..Thornton.. 08/02/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0328 AM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026

Valid 051200Z - 101200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Wednesday...

Broad troughing will exist from Hudson Bay into the north-central
U.S. with a belt of enhanced, cyclonic flow from the northern
Rockies through northern and central Plains into the upper Great
Lakes. At the surface, a front will advance through the upper Great
Lakes with the western extension of the boundary settling more
slowly south through the central into southern High Plains. 
Thunderstorms may be ongoing at 12Z across portions of the mid MO
Valley with lingering clouds and convective outflow potentially
modulating the location of the effective surface front and the
degree of instability ahead of it. The models suggest an area from
eastern KS into MO as being the most probable location for at least
isolated severe storms during the afternoon and evening hours. The
extent of the threat will likely be dependent on mesoscale details
yet to be known. As such, no area will be delineated in this
forecast.

Other areas of isolated severe storm potential will be in the
central High Plains and southeast AZ.


...Days 5 and 6/ Thursday and Friday...

A slight eastward shift of the mean trough position is forecast on
Thursday with some model signal for an embedded short-wave trough to
move through the Great Lakes. At the surface, there is some
suggestion that a weak front or wind shift will move into the
northern Mid-Atlantic during the afternoon with the trailing
extension of that boundary stretching through the mid MS Valley into
the southern High Plains. Ahead of that boundary, widespread 70+ F
dewpoints are expected from New England into the Mid-Atlantic and
Carolinas, leading to moderate to potentially strong instability.
The greatest potential for a few severe storms appears to be across
the Mid-Atlantic Thursday afternoon where the moderate instability
will coincide with a belt of 30-40 kt mid-level flow.

Some severe weather threat may also develop in the Ozark Plateau and
AZ Thursday afternoon and evening.  
 
On Friday, the above-mentioned Great Lakes short-wave trough is
expected to shear northeast across southern ON with 30-40 kt of
mid-level flow prevailing over the Northeast. The surface pattern is
somewhat disorganized with some semblance of a trough from southern
New England through the Mid-Atlantic coastal region. Moderate to
strong instability may again develop ahead of that feature,
supporting the potential for some severe weather threat during the
afternoon and early evening hours. However, the strongest vertical
shear is forecast to remain to the north of the stronger
instability, leading to uncertainty in the magnitude of the severe
threat.


...Days 7 and 8/Saturday and Sunday...

The various 00Z ensemble mean solutions indicate a slight eastward
shift of an upper low near Hudson Bay with low-amplitude troughing
and strengthening mid-level flow moving into the Northeast.
Southerly low-level winds within the western periphery of a surface
high positioned off the Atlantic Coast will maintain a moist and
unstable air mass beneath the strengthening winds aloft. As such,
some severe weather threat is expected to persist from the
Mid-Atlantic into New England this period.

Elsewhere, there is some model signal for a surface front to move
into the Midwest, where some severe weather potential may exist.

..Mead.. 08/02/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0249 PM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026

Valid 022000Z - 031200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE EAST
AS WELL AS PARTS OF THE SOUTHWEST AND NORTHERN PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered strong to locally severe thunderstorm development is
expected this afternoon and evening across parts of the lower Great
Lakes and upper Ohio Valley into the middle and southern Atlantic
Piedmont. Damaging winds are the primary hazard, although a tornado
could occur.

...20Z Update...
Only minor changes were made with this update. The MRGL Risk was
expanded slightly eastward in portions of eastern SC, where an
ongoing cluster of thunderstorms will continue to pose a risk of
damaging wind gusts, given a very warm/moist downstream air mass.
Farther north, the MRGL Risk was expanded into parts of northern NJ
and northeast PA. Clouds breaks have supported modest
destabilization of a moist air mass, and high-resolution guidance
depicts thunderstorms moving into the area tonight -- focused along
a northward-moving warm front. Despite modest instability, enhanced
low-level flow/shear overspreading the region in tandem with the
warm front could support a couple loosely organized cells/clusters
with an accompanying risk of damaging wind gusts and perhaps a brief
tornado. Elsewhere, the forecast remains on track and no changes
were needed.

..Weinman.. 08/02/2026

.PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1116 AM CDT Sun Aug 02 2026/

...Eastern States...
Current satellite imagery shows a positively titled shortwave trough
extending from Lower MI southwestward into the Mid-South, while
recent surface analysis places a corridor of low pressure associated
with this shortwave from the Middle OH Valley into the Lower Great
Lakes. Several surface lows are embedded within this broader area of
low pressure, including a primary low over north-central OH/western
Lake Erie. A cold front extends southward from this low to the TN/NC
border vicinity before arcing back more southwestward through
central AL and southern MS. 

This system (i.e. both the shortwave trough and associated cold
front) is forecast to gradually push eastward while weakening.
Airmass preceding this system is very moist, evidenced by upper
60s/low 70s dewpoints and PW values at or above 2 inches on the
regional 12Z soundings. Widespread cloud cover is in place, but
ample moisture has already resulted in airmass destabilization,
although the overall buoyancy will remain muted by poor lapse rates.
General expectation is for thunderstorm coverage to increase
substantially over the next few hours, fostered by a combination of
low-level confluence and modest large-scale ascent. 

Low to mid-level flow throughout the eastern periphery of the
shortwave trough is generally expected to be modest, ranging from
around 40 kt across the Allegheny Plateau/upper Ohio Valley/lower
Great Lakes vicinity to 20 kt across GA and SC. Consequently, a few
more organized storms are possible across portions of the Allegheny
Plateau, upper Ohio Valley, and lower Great Lakes, while a largely
disorganized multicellular mode is anticipated elsewhere.  
Water-loaded downbursts are the primary risk, although low-level
shear/SRH in the presence of a moist boundary layer suggests a brief
tornado is possible where greater storm organization is 
expected.

...North Dakota/northwest Minnesota...
Expansive upper ridging exists from southern CA/western AZ through
the Plains and into Manitoba and Ontario. A strong shortwave trough
is forecast to progress through Canadian Prairie Provinces within
the northern periphery of this ridging. A cold front associated with
this wave is expected to push eastward across the Dakotas,
interacting with a moistening airmass across the region. A
conditional risk for severe thunderstorms exists this afternoon, but
most of the guidance keeps the airmass capped and free of deep
convection. Better potential for thunderstorm development is
expected overnight and into tomorrow morning as large-scale ascent
attendant to the approaching shortwave combines with warm-air
advection to foster elevated thunderstorm development. Isolated
instances of hail and a strong gust or two are possible with these
storms.

...Southeast Arizona/far southwest New Mexico... 
Widely scattered thunderstorms should develop over the
mountains/higher terrain of the central/southern Arizona/New Mexico
border vicinity this afternoon. Moderate easterly/northeasterly
mid-level flow should favor southwestward motion into the lower
terrain of southeast Arizona. Modest buoyancy should allow for storm
persistence across southeast AZ, including the potential for
isolated strong to severe gusts.
